sahneler.metin: Is there *a piano* inside your ear?
cumleler: Is there a piano inside your ear?
At the base, the basilar membrane is narrow and stiff.
Toward the apex, it becomes wider and more flexible.
So high sounds vibrate at the base, low sounds near the apex.
On a piano, short tight strings play high, long loose strings low.
This frequency arrangement is called tonotopy.
